set.body:
Need (storyatlas4s Recall Voyage, 2026-09-03): a static SVG from intaglio cannot carry hover text.
The voyage plate names every mark (`data-name` = MarkId) but the words behind a mark — the recall
unit's text, the anchor's mass — only reach a reader through the Scala.js shell (Laminar hover
card). The owner opened the static edition and saw a plate with no tooltips. A browser and every
screen reader already understand a `<title>` child; intaglio has no per-grob channel for one.
Today `SvgOptions.title`/`description` exist only at document level (SvgRenderer.scala:164-174).

Proposal: an optional `title: Option[String]` (and `description`) on every `Grob` case, or a
`Grob.labelled(grob, title, description)` wrapper that the SVG backend lowers to `<title>`/`<desc>`
as the first children of the element or group; Canvas/Java2D/JavaFX ignore it for painting and may
expose it through hit-testing. Text is escaped like `escapeText`; determinism and byte-identity laws
extend to it; conformance requires the other backends to accept it without error.

Acceptance:
- a named grob with a title renders `<g data-name="…"><title>…</title>…</g>` (or the element form);
- a grob without a title renders byte-identically to today;
- laws: escaping of `<`, `&`, `]]>`; determinism across JVM and JS; `SceneConformance` unchanged;
- storyatlas4s `VoyageLowering` can set the unit's words as the title so `voyage.svg` has tooltips
  with no script.
set.title: [Intaglio 1.x][Accessibility][SVG] Per-grob title and description, emitted as <title>/<desc>
